page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a compute-focused server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 124 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.88 GB of memory per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the server exhibits exceptional single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, as evidenced by top-tier Geekbench multi-core results and strong PassMark CPU scores. Cryptographic and vector processing are accelerated by hardware support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions. Memory performance is solid, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 103.22 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 67.85 GB/sec.

Given its high-performance AMD EPYC cores and balanced memory allocation, the c4d-standard-32 is highly efficient for compute-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, text and image processing, and static web serving. Additionally, it demonstrates strong capabilities for small-scale LLM inference, particularly in text generation. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-effective choice for stateless compute clusters, CI/CD pipelines, and distributed processing nodes where external block storage is utilized.
